title: Should the 21 headings in the language reference that still hold an em dash lose it, with their links repointed?
today: On 10 August you ruled that the site's own text carries no em dash, and a test enforces it. On 2 November you extended that rule to the language reference, the project's own description of COMTRAN that the site publishes as reference pages. That change took 944 dashes out of it, but held back the headings. 21 headings still hold an em dash, and 10 contents lines repeat them, so readers of the reference pages still see the mark in those places.
why_now: The headings were held back because a heading's text sets its anchor, the link address after the # sign. Changing one changes the address, so every link to it must change in the same edit, and that needed its own decision. Draft PR 192 has made the change and passes every check. It waits only on your answer.
if_nothing: The headings keep the dash, and the site rule keeps a standing exception for headings and their contents lines. PR 192 stays open as a draft.

options.label: Change them and repoint every link
options.what_changes: Merge PR 192. 21 headings take a colon or a comma, for example "4.3 The SET command: arithmetic assignment". The 10 contents links move to the new addresses. The reference then keeps em dashes only in quotations, code, citation brackets and four table cells that hold the mark alone.
options.cost_risk: 21 anchors change once. An outside bookmark to an old anchor opens at the top of the page instead. Two close-out edits, to the site style record and the handover note, go in before the merge.
options.reverse: Easy: one revert commit restores the headings and links.
options.example: "### 4.3 The SET command — arithmetic assignment" becomes "### 4.3 The SET command: arithmetic assignment"; its contents link changes from #43-the-set-command--arithmetic-assignment to #43-the-set-command-arithmetic-assignment.

options.label: Keep them
options.what_changes: Close PR 192. The 21 headings and 10 contents lines keep the em dash on the reference pages.
options.cost_risk: Readers keep seeing the mark you ruled out. The no-em-dash rule keeps a written exception for headings. Changing later costs the same as now.
options.reverse: Easy: the change can be made at any later time; the prototype's approach still applies.

recommendation: Change them. It finishes the ruling you made on 2 November, and the only reason the headings were held back was the link risk, which PR 192 has dealt with. A search of the whole repository finds none of the 21 old anchors left, and a test checks that every link in the generated reading copy resolves. The one cost is that an outside bookmark to an old heading opens at the page top, which is small and happens once.
prototype: Draft PR 192 replaces the em dash in 21 language-reference headings with a colon or comma, repoints the 10 contents links, and regenerates the reading copy; all five checks pass and it is mergeable.
